newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish unemployment seen flat in November, to rise later.
newsitem.headline: Polish unemployment seen flat in November, to rise later.

text.p: Polish unemployment in November was not significantly different from October's 13.2 percent according to preliminary, unverified data, acting Labour Minister Maciej Manicki said on Friday.
Manicki told a news conference the number of unemployed was likely to rise towards the end of the year as well as in January and February next year, as seasonal jobs come to an end.
"November (unemployment rate) will not, in any significant way, differ from October," Manicki said.
"I expect the number of jobless at the end of the year to be just above 2.3 million and rising towards 2.4 million in January and February," he said.
In October there were 2.286 million unemployed, which constituted 13.2 percent of the workforce.
The labour ministry said official data on November unemployment would be released on December 19.
